lessons.title: System design fundamentals
lessons.creator: freeCodeCamp
lessons.description: Start with the questions that turn an ambiguous idea into a dependable system.
notes: Separate functional requirements (what the system does) from quality attributes (latency, durability and availability).
Estimate peak requests per second, payload sizes and storage growth. State your assumptions before calculating.
Sketch a client, API service and database. Add components only when a requirement justifies the complexity.
lessons.exercise: Design a service for sharing short text posts. List three functional requirements and three measurable quality targets.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Load balancing & horizontal scaling
lessons.creator: ByteByteGo
lessons.description: Distribute traffic, remove single points of failure, and make growth predictable.
notes: A load balancer routes traffic to healthy instances. Health checks should indicate whether an instance can actually serve requests.
Round-robin is simple; least-connections can handle uneven request duration. Sticky sessions complicate failover.
Keep application servers stateless so any healthy instance can serve the next request. Move shared state to durable storage.
lessons.exercise: Sketch a load balancer with three application servers. Explain what happens when one server fails.

lessons.title: Databases, indexes & storage
lessons.creator: freeCodeCamp
lessons.description: Choose a data model from access patterns, then reason about its tradeoffs.
notes: Start with the read and write queries, then choose tables and indexes to support them.
Indexes improve selected reads but increase write cost and storage. A composite index depends on column order.
Replication improves availability and read capacity; sharding distributes data but makes joins and rebalancing harder.
lessons.exercise: Model users, videos and comments. Pick indexes for retrieving recent comments for a video.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Caching & content delivery
lessons.creator: freeCodeCamp
lessons.description: Bring frequently requested data closer to the people who need it.
notes: Cache-aside reads check the cache before storage and populate the cache after a miss.
Set expiry based on acceptable staleness. Invalidate or version entries after updates.
Prevent a cache stampede with request coalescing and jittered expiry. CDNs cache assets near users.
lessons.exercise: Choose cache keys and expiry rules for video metadata. Explain how updates become visible.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Design a video streaming platform
lessons.creator: freeCodeCamp
lessons.description: Connect uploads, asynchronous processing, storage, and global delivery.
notes: Upload video directly to object storage using scoped upload URLs. Track metadata separately.
Use a durable queue to trigger transcoding into multiple resolutions. Make processing idempotent.
Deliver segments through a CDN. Track processing state so viewers only see playable content.
lessons.exercise: Draw the upload and playback paths. Discuss retries, failed transcoding jobs and regional failures.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Reliability & distributed tradeoffs
lessons.creator: freeCodeCamp
lessons.description: Design for partial failure and explain where consistency matters.
notes: A timeout does not prove a remote operation failed. Retried writes need an idempotency key.
Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Circuit breakers help prevent cascading overload.
Define recovery objectives and test restoration. Replicas alone do not replace backups.
lessons.exercise: A payment request times out after reaching the provider. Explain how to retry without charging twice.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Object-oriented thinking in Java
lessons.creator: Java Design Patterns tutorial
lessons.description: Model responsibilities and behavior with small, focused objects.
notes: Encapsulation keeps invariants inside the object that owns the data. Prefer behavior methods over public mutable fields.
Use interfaces for substitutable behavior. Prefer composition when inheritance does not represent a stable is-a relationship.
Separate domain logic from input/output so it can be tested without a database or web server.
lessons.exercise: Model a library loan. Decide which object prevents a book from being loaned twice.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: SOLID principles, made practical
lessons.creator: Geekific
lessons.description: Build Java code that is easier to extend, test, and reason about.
notes: Single responsibility means a coherent reason to change, not necessarily one method per class.
Depend on narrow interfaces at boundaries. Inject implementations rather than constructing dependencies deep in business logic.
Subtypes must preserve expected behavior. Adding an unsupported operation exception often signals a poor abstraction.
lessons.exercise: Refactor a notification service so adding SMS does not require editing the core delivery workflow.

lessons.title: Strategy & factory patterns
lessons.creator: Java Design Patterns tutorial
lessons.description: Make interchangeable behavior explicit and keep object creation understandable.
notes: A strategy encapsulates a family of algorithms behind a common interface.
A factory centralizes selection and construction; avoid factories when a constructor is already sufficient.
Inject a strategy into its consumer and test the consumer with a predictable fake implementation.
lessons.exercise: Implement a checkout service supporting flat-rate and percentage discounts.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Observer & event-driven objects
lessons.creator: Java Design Patterns tutorial
lessons.description: Decouple event producers from the objects that respond to them.
notes: Observers subscribe to an event source and receive notifications when state changes.
Specify whether callbacks are synchronous and what happens if a subscriber throws an exception.
Unsubscribe unused listeners to avoid retaining objects indefinitely. Avoid modifying the listener list while iterating.
lessons.exercise: Design a stock-price feed with email and console subscribers.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: State pattern & domain workflows
lessons.creator: Java Design Patterns tutorial
lessons.description: Represent valid transitions and make invalid actions impossible to overlook.
notes: Represent each lifecycle state explicitly, using an enum for simple cases or state objects for complex behavior.
Keep transition validation close to the aggregate that owns the state.
Write a transition table and test every allowed and forbidden action, including repeated requests.
lessons.exercise: Model a vending machine with idle, funded and dispensing states.
lessons.videoNote: Companion course — covers several topics in this learning path.

lessons.title: Design review & extensibility
lessons.creator: Geekific
lessons.description: Evaluate a design through requirements, invariants, and concrete change scenarios.
notes: Start a review by checking the required use cases rather than counting design patterns.
State invariants and ownership boundaries. Look for mutable data shared across unrelated objects.
Try one plausible new requirement and identify which classes change. Prefer clear code over speculative abstractions.
lessons.exercise: Review a parking-lot design for multiple vehicle types, pricing policies and concurrent entry.

challenges.title: Parking lot
challenges.description: Design a parking lot that assigns suitable spaces and calculates parking fees.
requirements: Support cars and motorcycles with appropriate spot types.
Issue a ticket on entry and release the spot on exit.
Reject entry when no compatible spot is free.
Calculate fees through a replaceable pricing policy.
hints: Separate ParkingSpot, Ticket, Vehicle and PricingPolicy.
Test a full lot, repeated exits, and incompatible vehicle types.

challenges.title: Notification service
challenges.description: Build an extensible notification system with interchangeable delivery channels.
requirements: Support email and SMS through a common interface.
Validate recipients before delivery.
Allow a new channel without modifying the core service.
Use a fake sender to test delivery without network access.
hints: Inject a NotificationChannel into your service.

challenges.title: Vending machine
challenges.description: Model a vending machine with clear states and reliable inventory handling.
requirements: Select an available product and accept payment.
Reject insufficient payment and return change.
Support cancellation before dispensing.
Prevent dispensing an out-of-stock product.
hints: Keep inventory changes atomic within a purchase.

challenges.title: LRU cache
challenges.description: Implement a bounded least-recently-used cache in Java.
requirements: Implement get and put with average O(1) complexity.
Evict the least recently used key at capacity.
Updating a key should refresh its recency.
Reject nonpositive capacity and test capacity one.
hints: Combine a HashMap with a doubly linked list or use LinkedHashMap.
Test misses, updates and repeated access before eviction.

challenges.title: Elevator system
challenges.description: Model multiple elevators and dispatch requests with a replaceable scheduling policy.
requirements: Support internal floor selection and external direction requests.
Track current floor, direction and door state.
Make dispatch policy replaceable.
Reject requests outside the building floor range.
hints: Separate dispatch decisions from elevator movement.
Test idle elevators and requests in opposite directions.

challenges.title: Split expenses
challenges.description: Design a shared-expense ledger with transparent balances.
requirements: Support equal and exact amount splits.
Validate that split amounts sum to the expense.
Track net balances per participant.
Settle debts without losing the expense history.
hints: Represent currency with BigDecimal rather than double.
Test rounding, self-payments and invalid totals.
